parsed.explanation: No criminalisation of same-sex activity or gender expression and no documented facility ban or birth-sex border rule. Tourism bodies publicly welcome LGBT visitors, and Pride has run since 2003. Against this, police targeting of trans women is documented: extortion, abuse, and a city practice of forcing trans sex workers to bathe in dirty river water and leave the area, with no recourse shown. Street harassment is well documented, though the case counts are monitoring figures, not rates. The 38% arrest survey has an unstated sampling frame, so I give it little weight. The prison statement is surgery-gated, unpublished and unverified, so it is an open question rather than an established exposure. UPR acceptances are not enacted law and carry no weight. Overall this is an elevated-risk profile driven by state-tolerated street targeting with thin recourse, partly offset by an absence of visitor-facing restrictions and documented tolerance in the capital.
